ca_spenders_opposing.spender: KEPNER FOR STATE SENATE 2026 SPONSORED BY LABOR ORGANIZATIONS; NURSES AND WORKING FAMILIES FOR

campaign_platform_points: Economy & cost of living: Scott will fight to lower the cost of housing, healthcare, childcare, groceries, and energy in the State Senate, building on his local record of streamlining regulations for multi-family and affordable homes, protecting renters, and securing funding for homelessness services.

Immigration: Drawing on his family's history in Japanese internment camps, Scott opposes ICE raids and will defend immigrants, LGBTQ+ Californians, reproductive freedom, seniors, and the social safety net including Medi-Cal and CalFresh in the State Senate.

Criminal justice & public safety: Scott advocates a balanced public safety approach combining more police staffing with community service workers, community-oriented policing, and emergency preparedness, while protecting civil rights. He credits this approach with declining crime and low use of force in Union City.

Education: Scott believes every child should have access to strong public schools and universal preschool, a conviction deepened by his wife's experience as a public school teacher. He will fight for universal access to education in the State Senate.

Civil liberties, privacy & surveillance: Scott supports innovation in AI, biotech, and clean energy but insists on strong public guardrails: protecting consumer privacy, preventing deepfakes and fraud, creating safeguards for children online, and adopting clear AI rules in employment, housing, lending, and public services.

Environment & climate: Scott will fight for lower energy costs, cleaner air, and a climate strategy that protects working families and future generations, building on his local record of updating climate action plans, expanding electric buses, and securing funding for transit and bike lanes.

Housing: Build far more housing at every level, especially infill and transit-oriented housing near jobs and transit hubs. Speed up approvals for projects meeting objective standards, expand adaptive reuse, and pursue a larger public-sector role in housing production including social-housing-style financing.

Healthcare: Move California toward universal healthcare by strengthening Medi-Cal, expanding access to care, lowering prescription drug costs, enforcing behavioral health parity, and protecting healthcare access from federal attacks so no Californian is left without affordable coverage.

campaign_platform_points: Homelessness: The campaign commits to cutting unsheltered homelessness in half over five years, building 1,600 affordable housing units (800 for homeless), connecting people to mental health and addiction services, cleaning up encampments, and providing emergency shelter.

Criminal justice & public safety: The campaign advocates a comprehensive, community-focused public safety strategy combining gun violence reduction (Operation Ceasefire), prevention programs, police academies, and anti-trafficking efforts, citing homicides at a 58-year low and violent crime down 22%.

Housing: The campaign pledges to expand affordable and accessible housing across Oakland, with 1,600 units in construction or breaking ground in 2026, including units set aside for people leaving homelessness and senior housing.

Government accountability & ethics: The campaign is finalizing a Charter Reform vision through a working group co-chaired by League of Women Voters and SPUR, aiming to improve transparency, efficiency, and accountability in City government after gathering input from over 1,150 residents.

Economy & cost of living: The campaign prioritizes reducing red tape for small businesses by fast-tracking permits, expanding same-day digital approvals, and streamlining zoning clearance to attract and retain businesses in commercial corridors like Downtown and Broadway Valdez.

Immigration: The campaign prohibits use of city property for federal immigration enforcement, orders OPD not to act at the direction of the National Guard or federal authorities, and established a citywide task force to protect residents' civil rights.

Environment & climate: The campaign commits to escalating cross-department wildfire operations, maintaining all fire stations open and operational, clearing high-risk brush with goats, and securing state grants to expand fire coverage in East Oakland hills.

Other: The campaign invests in youth programs including expanding the Mayor's Summer Youth Employment Program to 1,050 young Oaklanders, reopening the Mosswood Recreation Center, and restoring OPD Cadets as a career pathway for young adults.

campaign_platform_points: Education: Community colleges must serve the entire community, not just an elite few, including first-generation students, immigrant students, veterans, and lifelong learners at every stage of life.

Immigration: Harris will ban ICE from community college campuses, advocate for free immigration legal help on campuses, and protect students' personal records and information from immigration enforcement.

Education: Expand resources to protect low-income and historically disadvantaged student communities, provide inclusive mental health and counseling services, and keep nondiscrimination protections and inclusive workplace policies up to date.

Economy & cost of living: Make college more affordable by expanding financial aid, providing free meal programs, expanding WiFi access, offering free or discounted public transportation, expanding childcare, and working toward free community college tuition.
Housing: Partner with state and local governments to build affordable housing so that students and faculty can afford to live in the community where they work and learn.

Jobs & labor: Invest in career and technical education, apprenticeships, transfer pathways, and partnerships while ensuring workers have a voice when new technologies such as AI and automation affect their jobs.
Education: Opposes replacing instructors, faculty, or other campus workers with artificial intelligence. Calls for guardrails against AI in every level of government to protect students and workers.

Government accountability & ethics: Support independent audits to ensure funds are spent responsibly and efficiently, release audit findings to the public in accessible formats, and keep all meeting agendas, documents, and voting records publicly available.
